learning_outcomes.description: Explain plant structure and function in context of evolution and adaptation to diverse environments
As an individual or part of a student team design and/or perform experiments addressing well-defined questions in plant biology
Explain internal signalling and plasticity of plants
Evaluate the interactions of plants with other organisms
Describe current plant molecular biology approaches and evaluate regulatory frameworks

learning_activities.topic:
Lecture schedule

A detailed list of lectures and practicals can be found in the blackboard site for this course.


Sub-activity: - Introduction, Plant form and function, Plant evolution: mosses, ferns and other non-vascular and seedless plants (Dr Peter Crisp) - Plant Evolution: flowering plants, Plant Diversity and distributions, Plant names, classification and identification, Biodiversity (A/Prof Lyn Cook) - Introduction to plant hormones, Plant growth and development (Dr Anne Sawyer) - Plant resources: light and water, Plant resources: nutrients (Dr Nicole Robinson) - Fungi and Plant Interactions, Fungi and Plant Diseases (Dr Don Gardiner) - Plant Biotechnology (Dr Peter Crisp)

Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04, L05
